neighbours.label: The lead-in of fixed expressions containing 'it', such as 'what it takes' or 'worth it'.
fire: The coach asked whether Maya had what it takes to finish the race.
The long climb was absolutely worth it for the view from the summit.
The grant follows a use-it-or-lose-it policy at the end of the year.
Believe it or not, the tiny boat crossed the entire lake.
We wondered if the new team had what it takes to win the contract.
The repairs cost a fortune, but they were totally worth it.
The company treats the budget as a spend-it-or-lose-it allowance.
Believe it or not, she solved the puzzle in a minute.
quiet: The coach asked whether Maya had the determination to finish the race.
The long climb was absolutely worthwhile for the view from the summit.
The grant follows a spend-or-forfeit policy at the end of the year.
Surprisingly, the tiny boat crossed the entire lake.
We wondered if the new team had the ability to win the contract.
The repairs cost a fortune, but they were totally worthwhile.
The company treats the budget as a spend-or-forfeit allowance.
Amazingly, she solved the puzzle in a minute.

notes: Card peaks include what before it takes, WORTH before IT, lose before it, and Believe before It Or Not. Tests cover those constructions with paraphrases that retain the topic.
